cluster_name: Norway's King Harald V dies at 89, Haakon VIII ascends throne
tldr: At the title layer, reform-legacy framing is the single most prevalent signal: thirteen outlets across six language groups embed the word 'reform' or its equivalents — or describe Harald as a 'symbol' or a 'wise elder' — making cultural-legacy the dominant advertised frame before a reader clicks. The succession/Haakon-introduction frame is equally pervasive but draws a distinct cluster of outlets (Spain, Colombia, Taiwan, Germany's public broadcasters, NDTV) that lead with the transfer of power rather than mourning. The most analytically striking headline-body divergence is the near-total suppression of scandal: body text across AFP, the Guardian, Fox News, and Breitbart all surface Epstein and the rape conviction prominently, yet only France 24 Spanish and Iraqi News make scandal visible at title level — confirming it is an editorial choice made deliberately below the fold. Four country groups — China, Russia, Ukraine, and France — produced purely factual death-announcement headlines with no mourning language, no reform framing, and no succession emphasis, rendering their coverage invisible to any frame-based scanning at the homepage level.
event_summary: King Harald V of Norway died at Oslo University Hospital on August 28, 2026, aged 89, from haemolytic anaemia; his 53-year-old son Crown Prince Haakon immediately ascended the throne as King Haakon VIII.

silences.what_they_covered_instead: CGTN ran a title-only bulletin ('Norway's King Harald V dies at 89') with no mourning language, no reform framing, and no succession emphasis — a bare factual marker indistinguishable from a wire alert, revealing no editorial angle at the headline layer.

RT's headline ('Norway's King Harald V dead aged 89') is a minimal death announcement with no diplomatic register, no tribute language, and no contextual framing — consistent with the body-text pattern of institutional indifference toward a NATO-neighbour royal event.

Kyiv Post ran a plain death announcement ('Norway's King Harald Dead at 89') with no succession, mourning, or legacy angle visible at headline level despite Ukraine's close diplomatic ties with Norway.

France Info's headline ('Harald V, roi de Norvège depuis plus de trente ans, est mort à l'âge de 89ans') is a factual death notice noting only reign duration; no reform framing, no mourning language, and no succession angle appear at title level.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only outlet to make Harald's own words the headline: 'Quote of the Day by King Harald: Individuals shall not destroy the vast majority who want fellowship.' This editorial format — a philosophical prompt rather than a death-event announcement — is unique in the corpus and foregrounds Harald's values at the RSS/homepage layer rather than the news event.

The most scandal-prominent headline in the entire corpus at title level: 'el nuevo rostro de una monarquía envuelta en desgracias y escándalos' (the new face of a monarchy engulfed in misfortunes and scandals). This is the only non-English outlet — and one of only two outlets total — to surface the scandal frame at headline layer, where most editors suppressed it to body text.

Led with a direct-quote headline embedding the public-grief response: '"Eine ganze Nation trauert": Norwegens König Harald ist tot' (An entire nation mourns). The framing device — grief as the headline's quoted premise — is unique among German-language outlets, which otherwise led with new-king or death-announcement headlines.

The only headline in the corpus to frame the story around Queen Sonja's personal loss: 'Con la muerte del rey Harald V, Sonia de Noruega pierde a su gran amor' (Sonja of Norway loses her great love). This human-interest angle — Harald dying one day before their 58th wedding anniversary — is absent from all other outlets at title level.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, reform-legacy framing is the broadest single signal: thirteen outlets spanning six language groups label Harald 'reform-minded,' a 'symbol,' or invoke his 'contract' with the Norwegian people, a consistency absent from any single body-text frame in the same corpus. The succession/Haakon frame is equally pervasive but draws a distinct set of outlets. The clearest headline-body divergence is the scandal suppression: body text across AFP, the Guardian, Fox News, and Breitbart all surface Epstein and the rape conviction prominently, yet only France 24 Spanish and Iraqi News make this visible at title level, revealing it as a deliberate below-the-fold editorial choice rather than a universally foregrounded angle.
